title: Lemurian Tongue
subtitle: Test your understanding of Lemurian Tongue — the singular universal language and the Babel event that fractured it into mutually unintelligible dialects.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.body: The Lemurian Tongue was the singular universal language spoken across the entire physical plane. The Babel event fractured that speech, and recognizing this baseline exposes modern linguistic, national, and religious boundaries as recent administrative constructs.

questions.question: What primary function did the Lemurian Tongue serve prior to custodial post-reset intervention?

options.label: A
options.text: Serving as an exclusive dialect reserved strictly for temple priesthoods during Zep Tepi, stopping the explanation at that boundary alone.
options.rationale: The Lemurian Tongue was spoken globally by all human populations as a single universal language rather than being restricted to an elite priesthood.

options.label: B
options.text: It enabled all human populations to communicate without friction, cognitive distortion, or structural misunderstanding.
options.rationale: As a unified linguistic frequency, the Lemurian Tongue enabled all human populations to communicate without friction, cognitive distortion, or structural misunderstanding.

options.label: C
options.text: Establishing coded administrative protocols for the early custodial workforce, and that is treated as the entire mechanism.
options.rationale: Custodial administrators introduced administrative structures later to manage fragmented populations rather than using the original universal language.

options.label: D
options.text: Facilitating automated translation between human speech and high-density frequency signals, as if no adjacent systems participated at all.
options.rationale: The language operated directly as a natural harmonic frequency within human vocalization rather than requiring translation mechanisms.

questions.hint: Think about how a single shared frequency eliminates friction in collective thought.
